body:
Full-codebase review, web finding. Verified by reading.

The web client has no push queue, so a rejected `push()` means the edit never happened — but only the item and ledger dialogs catch and show the failure. Everywhere else the rejection is an unhandled promise rejection and the user is told nothing: toggling an item's status, undo, deleting from a dialog (`onDelete(id).then(onClose)` with no catch leaves the dialog open and silent), creating a list, and the list-properties actions including rename, category order, duplicate and revoke.

Scenario: tick an item off with the network down — the row does not strike through, nothing is said, and the edit is gone.

Separately, `saveCategoryOrder` applies the new order to local state before the push and the seeding ref never re-seeds, so after a failed push the page keeps showing an order the server never received.

Fix direction: route these through the same inline error treatment the dialogs use, or a shared toast.
title: Web: a failed push is silently swallowed outside the two dialogs, so the edit is lost
